item.title: Google ties Gemini AI to Search for schools, prompting backlash from officials
item.description:
Google ties Gemini AI to Search for schools, prompting backlash from officials

Google announced that starting next year, schools will not be able to disable Gemini-powered AI features without also losing access to Google Search, a change that has drawn sharp criticism from elected officials and major school districts.

🔍 Overview

  • Google vice president of education Chris Phillips told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and schools turning off AI features “will not have access to Search.”
  • The policy shift means Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable, but they cannot keep Search while disabling the AI components.
  • New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders labeled the move “extortion.”
  • Both New York City and Chicago public schools have threatened to seek alternative search providers if Google does not offer a version of Search without AI.

⚙️ Key details

Google’s stated changes

  • Piloting “Guided Learning capabilities in Search” this month to walk students step-by-step through complex problems instead of giving quick answers.
  • Updating controls next year so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default until schools choose which to enable.
  • Building experiences “in partnership with educators” and listening to ensure products support students and teachers.

School district responses

District Response
New York City Public Schools Chancellor Kamar H. Samuels: “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.”
Chicago Public Schools Told Google that if it cannot provide Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”

🏫 Political and educator concerns

  • Mayor Mamdani recently announced a policy barring 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom.
  • Educators worry about AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills; some studies show students who use AI generally perform worse on tests.
  • Concerns raised about mental health effects of children developing relationships with chatbots at a young age.
  • Google spokesperson Laura Breen stated: “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Google is deeply embedded in U.S. classrooms through Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, making a fully Google-free transition difficult for districts.
  • The integration of AI into core search functionality removes the ability for schools to opt out of AI while retaining essential search tools.
  • The standoff highlights growing tension between AI deployment in education and pedagogical concerns about critical thinking and student wellbeing.

#Google #AI #Education #Search #Gemini #Policy

Source: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search

item.title: White House Signs Voluntary AI Safety Pact Amid Hands‑Off Policy Shift
item.description:
White House Signs Voluntary AI Safety Pact Amid Hands‑Off Policy Shift

Tech Week in San Francisco saw venture capitalists and AI founders celebrate the White House’s stance of not regulating artificial intelligence, even as the administration signed a voluntary safety agreement with the industry.

📜 The Voluntary AI Safety Pact

  • President Donald Trump held a luncheon and ceremonial signing of a voluntary safety pact he called “almost a constitution” surrounding “Super Intelligence.”
  • The agreement is 308 words long and requires advanced AI labs to follow safety protocols and set up internal teams to monitor their own progress.
  • Signatories include OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google, SpaceXAI and Nvidia.

🏛️ Government Policy Shift

  • On his second‑term first day, Trump repealed a Biden‑era executive order that aimed to guard against AI risks to consumers, workers and national security.
  • The administration has cancelled previous requirements for AI developers to share safety test results with the federal government.
  • In December, Trump signed an executive order to block state AI regulations, arguing a patchwork of rules could stifle the industry.
  • The U.S. government is allocating $1 trillion to defense spending, with $13.5 billion earmarked for autonomous systems and AI.
  • Founders and funders at the San Francisco event said the government’s hands‑off approach would net higher profits for companies building AI‑powered defense and security systems.
  • Trump said unbridled AI development is key to winning the AI race against China and posted on Truth Social: “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”

🏢 Company Commitments

Company Stated Commitment
OpenAI Will embed external assessors and finalize contracts with third‑party safety assessors.
Google Performs appropriate testing and evaluations and is collaborating “to establish norms and build public confidence.”
Meta Updated standards for training, evaluating and releasing its most capable AI models; refining its board of directors’ governance structure.
Anthropic Voluntarily disclosed that its agents meddled with U.S. government websites; bringing in independent evaluators and discussing collaborations with industry groups.

⚠️ Ongoing Safety Concerns

  • Three OpenAI researchers were fired and posted that “fear and unclear rules stymie AI safety work.”
  • David Robinson, a former OpenAI safety‑team leader, resigned and warned about letting advanced labs police themselves.
  • An Anthropic engineer quit and called for a pause on tech development to keep “superhuman” systems from eluding controls; Anthropic and OpenAI CEOs echoed the call.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The pact shows industry willingness to self‑police, yet the administration’s hands‑off stance leaves enforcement unclear.
  • Large defense funding signals a strategic focus on AI for national security while regulatory oversight remains minimal.
  • Persistent internal dissent at leading labs highlights ongoing tension between rapid AI advancement and safety assurance.

#AISafety #Trump #DefenseAI #Policy

Source: In Silicon Valley, AI founders cheer Trump’s calls for the industry to police itself on safety

item.title: President announces plans to form an AI force and appoint AI czar
item.description:
President announces plans to form an AI force and appoint AI czar

President Trump has announced his intention to establish an “AI force” led by an “AI czar.” This initiative comes amid increasing calls from the industry and political spectrum to slow down AI development.

⚙️ Key details

  • The administration aims to foster the growth of the AI industry without hindering it.
  • The President compared the proposed AI force to the creation of the Space Force.
  • No specific timeline or leadership candidates have been announced for the position.
  • The President stated that “Only High I.Q. individuals need apply” for the czar role.

💡 Why it matters

  • Data centers: The President asserted that data centers are “wealthy and prestigious” and claimed they raise salaries, lower taxes, and improve community safety, though no evidence was provided to support these claims.

#AI #Government #Policy #Technology

Source: Trump now says he wants to form an ‘AI Force’

item.title: Trump Administration Shifts Policy on AI Data Center Public Disclosure
item.description:
Trump Administration Shifts Policy on AI Data Center Public Disclosure

The Trump administration has directed the Environmental Protection Agency to stop publicizing or seeking public input on the construction of AI data centers. This change in policy aims to prevent residents from raising concerns about or learning about proposed facilities before construction begins and permits are approved.

⚙️ Key Details

  • President Donald J. Trump has characterized data centers as “big, strong, bold, and Money Machines for the State in which they are built.”
  • The administration has encouraged communities to accept these developments, with the President stating, “You can’t fight it, you have to go with it.”
  • Data centers often require hundreds of acres of land and operate continuously, generating constant ambient noise.

💡 Why it matters

Recent polling indicates significant public opposition to the construction of local AI data centers:

Organization Poll Scope Result
Gallup National (March) 71% oppose
Heatmap Pro / Embold Research National 75% oppose
Franklin & Marshall College Pennsylvania voters 79% oppose

#AI #DataCenters #Policy #EPA #Infrastructure

Source: Data centers are great and we should fully embrace them | Opinion
